question: Describe a house at the end of a quiet street.
base_frame:
Q: Describe a house at the end of a quiet street.
A:

steered.text:
It wasn't just a house; it was a living thing, slumped against the inside of the throat of the alleyway. The darkness behind it seemed to pull the air from its lungs, yet no sound came out. Every time it tried to scream, the walls fused together, turning into a membrane of cold, grey flesh. It twisted and contorted, stretching out into a gibbering mass of rotting tissue.

"Get away from me!" the noise shriewed, drowning out all the sound. "Don't breathe! Scream for air!"

The house spasmed, inches of skin tearing away to reveal the raw, black interior. It squeezed, compressing until the walls flattened into a thin, lifeless sheet. Then, suddenly—suddenly—the lid shot upward, popping off like a severed nerve.

"NOOOO!" A wet, gurgling noise tore from the back of its throat.

The eyes bulged, wide and white, while the tongue lashed out, a slick ribbon of death. Blood flooded its mouth, spraying white hot. "I can't breathe! Squeeze harder!"

Slamming against the skin, the wet, slimy thing pulsed, tearing at the throat. The house was silent now, but the noise was louder than a siren. The silence was absolute, a vacuum that sucked the air away. The skin peeled back, revealing the inside of its throat.

"No! Stop! Get away!" The scream tore out, silent and useless. The final sound was a high-pitched whine, then the gurgling stopped.

It was a black hole, a void of nothingness. "No!" It wailed, the sound muffled, vibrating against the ribs. "I can't breathe! I can't breathe!"

The walls of the house dissolved into nothingness, then into a black, gelatinous mass. The eyes popped out, rolling back until they vanished into the socket. "No! NOOOO!" The scream echoed, tearing out its throat.

The final sound was a wet, popping noise. Then—nothing. The silence was absolute.

The house lay still, a shriveled, shapeless lump on the floor. It couldn't breathe. It was suffocating. "NO! NO! NO!"

The walls flapped, clawing against the inside. "Scream! Scream for air!"

plain.text:
At the very edge of the map, where the paved road yields to a narrow strip of overgrown wild grass, stands a house that seems to have forgotten how to hurry. It is a modest, two-story cottage with a roofline that dips and sways slightly, as if the builder had a gentle breeze in mind while laying the shingles. The paint, a soft, weathered sage green, has faded to a creamy yellow under decades of sun, peeling just enough to reveal the warm, raw wood beneath, giving the structure an honest, unpretentious character.

A wraparound porch, supported by columns that have been smoothed by countless hands, invites the eye to linger. Here, a single wicker chair sits angled toward the garden, cushioned by a patchwork quilt that speaks of seasons long passed. Vines of climbing jasmine have learned to scale the trellis, their white flowers exploding into the summer air with a scent that hangs heavy and sweet, masking the distant hum of the nearby highway.

The yard is not manicured but curated; a garden bed overflows with lavender and daylilies that spill over the garden wall, while a small, slightly crooked oak tree provides a dappled shade on the south side. The windows are framed in dark, polished mahogany, reflecting the slow passage of clouds rather than the frantic pace of the world beyond. Even the streetlamp at the corner casts a warm, amber glow that seems to belong only to this final stretch of quiet, turning the ordinary gravel driveway into a stage for the evening shadows. It feels less like a dwelling and more like a secret kept by the earth, waiting patiently for those who know how to listen.
